title: STEERING KNUCKLE & FRT WHEEL HUB ASM STUDS & LWR CONT ARM BUMPER
summary: Front suspension: the upper and lower ball joints (ball stud assemblies) and the lower control arm rebound bumper, and how the steering knuckle/front hub (spindle) hangs on the ball studs. The ball joints are riveted to the control arms; each ball stud goes through the knuckle and is held by a castellated (slotted) nut and cotter pin; each ball joint has a grease (zerk) fitting. The rubber bumper is bolted to the lower control arm.

fastening.note: Upper ball joint [2] is riveted to the outer end of the upper control arm with rivets [14].

Upper ball stud goes down through the upper boss of the steering knuckle [4]; castellated nut [13] on the stud, locked with cotter pin [6]. Up to 90 lbs ft allowed to line the slot up with the cotter pin hole.
Lower ball joint [7] is riveted to the outer end of the lower control arm with rivets [3].

Lower ball stud goes up through the lower boss of the steering knuckle [4]; castellated nut [5] from below, locked with cotter pin [6]. Up to 125 lbs ft allowed to line the slot up with the cotter pin hole. View A: cotter pin eyelet tight in the nut slot and legs bent over.
Screw [9] goes down through the bumper [10] bracket and the lower control arm; nut [8] underneath. Must assemble in direction shown.
Lock washer [11] and nut [12] go on the threaded upper end of the lower ball joint [7], next to the bumper bracket, on top of the arm; the lube fitting [1] screws into the top of that end.
A lube fitting [1] screws into the top of each ball joint; grease 4b (upper) and 4c (lower).

notes: A torque of 90 lbs ft maximum is permissible on nut when slot is in correct position for insertion of cotter pin. (nut [13])
A torque of 125 lbs ft maximum is permissible on nut when slot is in correct position for insertion of cotter pin. (nut [5])
View A, cotter pin installation: Eyelet must be tight in nut slot & shaft, bent as shown, to prevent rotation or looseness which will interfere with camber-castor gage.
